newsitem.title: POLAND: EU mulls fund for Polish farm development by 1998.
newsitem.headline: EU mulls fund for Polish farm development by 1998.

text.p: The European Union is mulling launching a special fund by next year for the development of agricultural regions in Poland, EU farm commissioner Franz Fischler told daily Rzeczpospolita in its Saturday edition.
"It's hard to predict how quickly the proceeds would be released and how big they would be...but I think it (the fund) could happen already next year," Fischler was quoted as saying.
He said the proposal should show up in a discussion paper on EU financial perspectives starting in 1999 due this July.
Fischler said too little money was being directed to the development of Polish farming regions and agriculture.

"The initiation of such a policy on the development of the countryside is important because if it doesn't happen there's a real danger that in 10 to 20 years only old people will live in certain regions of the country," he said.

Fischler also said it was necessary to increase the participation of foreign firms in the development of the Polish food industry and to ensure that Polish farmers had access to modern financial instruments.
He said the biggest problem facing the integration of Polish agriculture with that of the EU was the subsidies Polish farmers receive from the government in pricing and exports.
"It's hard today to predict how many years after gaining (EU) membership Polish farmers would be rid of direct subsidies," Fischler said.
He said Poland would likely not become an EU member before 2003 due to the lengthy political process of approving new members rather than for reasons pertaining to agriculture.
